rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to these verses, and “the clear Book” is the one promised in the Torah; he compares the wording with 2:1.
rows.anchor: الذي وعدتم به في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “We sent it down” may refer either to the Book, sent down as Arabic recitation, or to the account of Joseph; qurʾān means something gathered.
rows.anchor: هذه الهاء تصلح لشيئين، أحدهما أن تكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jewish scholars reportedly told the pagan leaders to ask Muhammad why Jacob’s family moved to Egypt and about Joseph; this revelation answered them, as 12:7 indicates.
rows.anchor: لكبراء المشركين: سلوا محمدا لم انتقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We recount” means explaining with the finest clarity; a qāṣṣ tells a story truthfully, and “by what We revealed” means by revealing this Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: أي نبين لك أحسن البيان والقاص الذي يأتي بالقصة على حقيقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading of Qurʾānan is the transmitted reading; genitive as apposition or nominative as an explanatory gloss are linguistically possible but should not be recited.
rows.anchor: القراءة نصب القرآن ويجوز الجر والرفع جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was unaware of Joseph’s story and learned it only through revelation.
rows.anchor: أي من الغافلين عن فصة يوسف وإخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause with “when” may be accusative as the time of recounting, or an instruction to remember when Joseph spoke.
rows.anchor: المعنى نقص عليك إذ قال يوسف لأبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two case readings of yā abati are reported, and some Arab grammarians also permit yā abata.
rows.anchor: في قوله: (يا أبت إني) قراءتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the genitive form of yā abati, the possessive yā is deleted in address; the feminine tā is special to vocatives and replaces the possessive ending.
rows.anchor: لأن ياء الإضافة تحذف في النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feminine-marked forms can denote males as nouns or adjectives, as in ʿayn/nafs and ghulām yafʿa/rabʿa; pausing is yā abah despite the written tā.
rows.anchor: المذكر قد سمي باسم لمؤنث فيه علامة التأنيث

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says a kasra reading pauses with tā only, while a fatḥa reading may pause with tā or hāʾ; al-Zajjāj says the two cases do not differ.
rows.anchor: وزعم الفراء أنك إذا كسرت وقفت بالتاء لا غير

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub offers several explanations for fatḥa in yā abati, including shortening yā abatah and an appeal to a line attributed to al-Ṭirimmāḥ.
rows.anchor: وزعم قطرب أن الفتح على جهات: إحداها أنك أردت يا أبة ثم حذفت التنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects Quṭrub’s explanations: an inflected accusative vocative cannot lose tanwīn, and yā dāru aqwat is not transmitted with fatḥa or intelligible on that analysis.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله قطرب خطأ كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh, al-Khalīl, and Basrans transmitted yā dāru aqwat with ḍamma on dāl, not fatḥa.
rows.anchor: أنشد سيبويه والخليل وجميع البصريين يا دار أقوت، بضم الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā abatah is not a lament here; the permissible fatḥa instead reflects a deleted alif that replaced the possessive tā.
rows.anchor: فالندبة ههنا - لا معنى لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative yā abatu is weak because its hāʾ is serving as a substitute for the possessive yā.
rows.anchor: بالرفع فلا يجوز إلا على ضعف، لأن الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sukūn reading on ʿayn is also called sound and frequent.
rows.anchor: فأما التسكين في العين فقراءة صحيحة كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form aḥad aʿshar is very poor and unused, so it should be disregarded.
rows.anchor: أحد اعشر وهذه الرواية في الرداءة وترك الاستعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawkaban is accusative as specification (tamyīz).
rows.anchor: و (كوكبا) منصوب على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated raʾaytuhum reinforces the statement after a long intervening phrase.
rows.anchor: فكرر رأيتهم توكيدا، المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nonhumans take the masculine rational plural when described as worshipping or speaking; he illustrates this with the ant, the great idol, and celestial bodies.
rows.anchor: فإذا وصف غير الناس والملائكة بأنه يعبد ويتكلم فقد دخل في المميزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw/nūn plural marks nonhumans treated as discerning, while alif/tā marks feminine or inanimate non-discerners; their verbs follow the same distinction.
rows.anchor: والألف والتاء والنون لكل مؤنث ولكل موات لا يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatḥa on ʿayn is the undisputed standard; Sībawayh, al-Khalīl, and their colleagues allow only it, although Quṭrub and al-Farrāʾ report sukūn.
rows.anchor: فأما ما لا اختلاف فيه ففتح العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yajtabī means choose or select, derived from collecting something for oneself, as when water is collected in a basin.
rows.anchor: وهو مشتق من جبيت الشيء إذاحصلته لنفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in kathālika is accusative: God chooses Joseph in a manner like the interpretation of what he saw.
rows.anchor: نصب، المعنى ومثل مارأيت تأويله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl al-aḥādīth may mean dream interpretation or interpretation of prophets’ and nations’ accounts, that is, scriptures; both are valid.
rows.anchor: وقيل يعلمك تأويل أحاديث الأنبياء والأمم، يعني الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob had interpreted Joseph’s dream: eleven stars signified eminent, guiding people; the sun and moon were his parents, and the stars his brothers.
rows.anchor: فتأول الأحد عشر كوكبا أحد عشر نفسا لهم فضل وأنهم يستضاء بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation foretells that Joseph and his brothers will be prophets; completing God’s favor on them means making them prophets as with Abraham and Isaac.
rows.anchor: فتأول له أنه يكون نبيا، وأن إخوته يكونون أنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruʾyā has four forms: the hamzated and wāw forms are read, while the assimilated form and the form with kasra on rāʾ are not read.
rows.anchor: رؤيا بالهمز، ورويا بالواو بلا همز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūsuf and Yūnus each have forms with ḍamma or kasra on the medial consonant; Quṭrub’s form with fatḥa on Yūnus’s nūn is anomalous.
rows.anchor: ويوسف فيه لغتان، يوسف بضم السين ويوسف بكسر السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural āyāt was read; a singular āya was also read, meaning a lesson, and another codex reportedly had ʿibratan li-l-sāʾilīn.
rows.anchor: وقد رويت في غير هذا المصحف عبرة للسائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āya may mean a sign for those who questioned the Prophet, who answered about Joseph despite having been unaware and without reading a book; he knew by revelation.
rows.anchor: بصيرا للسائلين الذين سألوا النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers complain that their father prefers the two younger sons although their larger group is more useful; ʿuṣba means a clan or group.
rows.anchor: إن أبانا قدم اثنين صغيرين في المحبة علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that Jacob is in manifest error concerns his love for the two, not his religion; calling him religiously astray would make them unbelievers.
rows.anchor: إنما عنوا أن أباهم ضال في محبة هذين ولو وصفوه بالضلالة في الدين كانوا كفارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise to become righteous means they would repent after killing Joseph.
rows.anchor: أي تتوبون من بعد قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arḍan means a distant land, since Joseph would necessarily be somewhere on earth; yakhlu lakum wajhu abīkum shows they planned a place beyond Jacob’s reach.
rows.anchor: أرضا يبعد بها عن أبيه لأنه لن يخلو من أن يكون في أرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arḍan is accusative after omitting fī and making the verb govern it directly, since it is not an indefinite adverbial place noun.
rows.anchor: منصوب على إسقاط (في) وإفضاء الفعل إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghiyāba is anything hidden or concealed; al-Munkhil’s verse uses ghayyabatnī to illustrate the word.
rows.anchor: الغيابة كل ما غاب أو غيب عنك شيئا، قال المنخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jubb is an unlined well, named for having been dug without further construction such as lining.
rows.anchor: والجب البئر التي ليست بمطوية، وسميت جبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that Judah proposed not killing Joseph and was among the strongest of the brothers.
rows.anchor: ورووا أن اسم الذي أشار عليهم بألا يقتلوه يهوذا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan read taltaqiṭ-hu with feminine tā; grammarians allow it by treating baʿḍ al-sayyāra as a feminine singular caravan.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن تلتقطه بالتاء، وأجاز ذلك جميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians cite an unattributed line using the feminine verb shariqat as evidence for this agreement pattern.
rows.anchor: وأنشدوا: وتشرق بالقول الذي قد أذعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾmannā has four readings: nasal assimilation with lip-rounding, assimilation without it, two distinct nūns with a vowel, and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb’s taymanā.
rows.anchor: على إشمام الميم الضم - تأمننا، وعلى الإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb’s reading conflicts with the codex, though its kasra on tā and assimilation of identical consonants are grammatical.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى ابن وثاب تيمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lip-rounding signals the omitted ḍamma; leaving it unrounded is good because mīm is open, and pronouncing both nūns is good because they belong to separate words.
rows.anchor: والإشمام يدل على الضمة المحذوفة، وترك الإشمام جيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings vary between yartʿu/ nartʿ and yalʿab/ nalʿab, with yāʾ or nūn and with yāʾ carrying ḍamma; all are jussive responses to the command.
rows.anchor: بالياء، وقرئت (نرتع ونلعب) بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kasra on the ʿayn derives yartʿ from grazing; the phrase promises grazing and play, combining benefit with enjoyment.
rows.anchor: من الرعي، المعنى يرتعي ويلعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yartaʿ can also derive from ratʿa, meaning to live expansively in fertile abundance; anything abundant is rātiʿ.
rows.anchor: ويرتع من الرتعة، أي يتسع في الخصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wārid is the person who goes to water to supply his group.
rows.anchor: الوارد الذي يرد الماء ليسقي للقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adlaytu means lowering a bucket to fill it, while dalawtu means drawing it out.
rows.anchor: أدليت الدلو إذا أرسلتها لتملأها، ودلوتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā bushrāya is read with alif and open yāʾ, yā bushrī, or without the possessive yāʾ; the possessive ending normally alters what precedes, but alif is preferably unchanged.
rows.anchor: بألف وياء مفتوحة، وقرئت يا بشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling an inanimate or irrational thing is a way to alert listeners and heighten the account; yā bushrāya effectively means “rejoice, this is your moment.”
rows.anchor: ومعنى النداء في هذه الأشياء التي لا تجيب ولا تعقل إنما هو على تنبيه المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They concealed Joseph as merchandise, wanting others to think the water people had entrusted him to them; biḍāʿatan is a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: لما وجدوه أحبوا أن لا يعلم بأنه موجود، وأن يوهموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bakhs is explained as injustice, since a found person cannot lawfully be sold, or as a deficient price; most exegesis favors injustice.
rows.anchor: قيل بخس: ظلم، لأن الإنسان الموجود لا يحل بيعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports give the sale price as twenty, twenty-two (two dirhams from each brother), or forty dirhams.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أنه بيع بعشرين درهما، وقيل باثنين وعشرين درهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fīhi is not the complement of al-zāhidīn: the phrase first says they were ascetics, then identifies what they abstained from; this fronting is allowed for adverbials, not objects attached to a participle.
rows.anchor: ليست بصلة الزاهدين، المعنى: وكانوا من الزاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miṣr stays fatḥa in the genitive because it is the proper name of a specific city and is indeclinable.
rows.anchor: مصر مفتوحة في موضع الجر إلا أنها لا تنصرف، لأنها اسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathwāhu means his residence; the wife is told to treat Joseph well throughout his stay.
rows.anchor: مقامه. المعنى أحسني إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report names three people of exceptional discernment: the Egyptian official about Joseph, Shuʿayb’s daughter about Moses, and Abū Bakr in appointing ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن أفرس الناس ثلاثة، وأن أجودهم فراسة العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus We established Joseph” means in the same manner as what was just described.
rows.anchor: أي ومثل الذي وصفنا مكنا ليوسف في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching taʾwīl al-aḥādīth may mean dream interpretation or interpretation of prophetic accounts.
rows.anchor: جائز أن يكون تأويل الرؤيا، وأن يكون تأويل أحاديث الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd spans roughly age seventeen to forty; God made Joseph wise and knowledgeable, though knowledge alone does not make everyone wise.
rows.anchor: الأشد من نحو سبع عشرة سنة إلى نحو الأربعين، آتيناه حكما وعلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wise person uses what he knows and refrains from acting where he lacks knowledge; ḥakama originally means restrain, as a horse’s bit restrains it.
rows.anchor: الحكيم العالم المستعمل علمه، الممتنع من استعمال ما يجهل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards the good-doers as He described in teaching Joseph.
rows.anchor: ومثل ما وصفنا من تعليم يوسف نجزي المحسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She solicited Joseph for what women seek from men; the text’s omission of the explicit sexual act still makes clear what she sought.
rows.anchor: مما يريد النساء من الرجال، فعلم بتركه ذكر الفاحشة نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayta laka means “come here”; its most common form has fatḥa on tāʾ, and ʿAlī’s reported reading has the same sense.
rows.anchor: وفي (هيت لك) لغات: يجوز هيت لك، وهيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet’s lines use hayta as an invitation to come; Quṭrub reports a Hijazi recitation attributed to Ṭarafa with the same word.
rows.anchor: أن العراق وأهله. . . عنق إليك فهيت هيتا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly read haiʾtu laka with hamza and kasra, meaning “I have prepared myself for you,” from hayʾa.
rows.anchor: رويت عن ابن عباس هئت لك مهموزة مكسورة الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa form is like an interjection with no conjugated verb; kasra follows the default at two adjacent quiescent letters, while ḍamma reflects a deleted possessive in the sense “my invitation to you.”
rows.anchor: فلأنها بمنزلة الأصوات، ليس منها فعل يتصرف

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī’s reading hiʾtu laka is equivalent to hīta laka and has the same grammatical justification.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة هيت والحجة فيها كالحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿādh Allāh is a verbal noun meaning “I seek refuge in God,” as in ʿudhtu ʿiyādhan wa-maʿādhan.
rows.anchor: مصدر، المعنى أعوذ بالله أن أفعل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabbi refers to the Egyptian official; mathwāya means he cared for Joseph throughout his stay, so betraying his household would be wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي إن العزيز صاحبي (أحسن مثواي)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, rabbi may refer to God, who cared for Joseph throughout his stay.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «إنه ربي» يعني الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes say Joseph intended her until he saw Jacob’s image warning him against an act of fools while he was recorded among the prophets.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين أنه هم بها حتى رأى صورة يعقوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Joseph saw an inscription in the house forbidding adultery, citing 17:32.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه رأى في البيت مكتوبا:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj is certain Joseph saw a proof that stopped him from what he intended.
rows.anchor: ولسنا نشك أنه قد رأى برهانا قطعه عما هم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the syntax to mean that, had he not seen his Lord’s proof, Joseph would have intended her.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: المعنى (ولقد همت به وهم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exegetes’ account is that he did intend her and sat as a man sits with a woman, but God showed him the proof; 12:53 supports this reading.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه المفسرون أنه هم بها وأنه جلس منها مجلس الرجل من المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended meaning is that without seeing the proof he would have carried out his intention; the placement of lawlā after the response is unusual because it normally precedes a response marked with lām.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لولا أن رأى برهان ربه لأمضى ما هم به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Joseph the proof to turn evil and indecency away: evil here is betraying his patron, and indecency is committing fornication.
rows.anchor: أي كذلك أريناه البرهان لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on the lām, al-mukhlaṣīn are those God purified from evils, like the chosen; with kasra, they are those who made their religion sincere to God.
rows.anchor: وقرئت من المخلصين بكسر اللام، أي الذين أخلصوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf and the official’s wife raced to the door; qadd means to tear or rip the shirt from behind.
rows.anchor: يعني به يوسف وامرأة العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They found her master at the door, leaving her caught by her own stratagem; her proposed penalty was imprisonment or painful punishment.
rows.anchor: أي صادفا سيدها لدى الباب فحصرها في ذلك الوقت كيد لما فاجأت سيدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge means the only penalty for someone who sought evil with the household is prison or painful torment; alīm means painful.
rows.anchor: أي ما جزاؤه إلا السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says she was the one who sought him.
rows.anchor: أي هي التي أرادت السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness from her family is variously said to be a wise man or a child.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه رجل حكيم، وقيل إنه طفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tear in front proves she pushed him away as he approached; a tear in back proves he retreated while she followed.
rows.anchor: إن كان هو المقبل عليها وهي الدافعة له عن نفسها فيجب أن تكون خرقت قميصه من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings include min qabli/min duburi with tanwīn and forms without tanwīn treating before/behind as definite endpoints.
rows.anchor: والقراءة من قبل ومن دبر، ومن قبل ومن دبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatḥa on qabla and dubura is remote; Basrans allow treating them as definite, indeclinable forms, while Ibn Abī Isḥāq reportedly used fatḥa or ḍamma on qubl and fatḥa is more transmitted.
rows.anchor: أما الفتح فبعيد في قوله: من قبل ومن دبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The official identifies the wife’s statement “what is the penalty…” as her scheme.
rows.anchor: أي إن قولك: (ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا)

rows.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd says kāna retains its force because it denotes actions, even after the light conditional particle in in kāna.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد: " كان " لقوتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis treats kāna as future in meaning but expressed by a past form: if the shirt is found cut in front, the finding is what follows.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني أن " كان " عبارة عن الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Turn away from this” tells Joseph to conceal the affair and not mention it.
rows.anchor: معناه يا يوسف اكتم هذا الأمر ولا تذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Egyptian official was not very jealous.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنه كان قليل الغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Astakhliṣhu is jussive as the response to a command and means “make him exclusively mine,” with no one sharing him.
rows.anchor: جزم جواب الأمر، ومعنى أستخلصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king says he has recognized Joseph’s trustworthiness and innocence of the accusation.
rows.anchor: أي عرفنا أمانتك وبراءتك مما قرفت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khazāʾin al-arḍ means the kingdom’s stores or wealth; ḥafīẓ means guarding it and ʿalīm knowing how it should be managed.
rows.anchor: أي أحفظها وأعلم وجوه متصرفاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets establish truth and justice and place things properly; Joseph knew no one could do this better and requested the office to serve the common good.
rows.anchor: لأن الأنبياء بعثوا في قامة الحق والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for the brothers’ younger sibling follows an unstated prior exchange; the official likely asked about their news, family, and number.
rows.anchor: قد كان قبله كلام جر إليه ما يوجب طلب أخيهم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls himself the best host because he gave the visitors excellent hospitality when lodging them.
rows.anchor: لأنه حين أنزلهم أحسن ضيافتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn in taʾtūn and taqrabūn is read with kasra, with fatḥa also permitted as a plural nūn, as in 15:54; “do not approach me” is formally indicative but functions as a command.
rows.anchor: القراءة بكسر التون، ويجوز الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their assurance “we will do it” is emphatic.
rows.anchor: سنراود عنه أباه وإنا لفاعلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both fityānihi and fityatihi are read; in this context fityān/fiṭya means servants or slaves.
rows.anchor: والفتيان والفتية المماليك في هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the brothers would recognize their returned payment and know the food was free and Joseph had ordered it placed in their bags.
rows.anchor: إذا رأوا بضاعتهم مردودة عليهم، علموا أن ما كيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, lʿallahum yarjiʿūn means they might return the payment, which was the price of their food, since they would not take anything without paying.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون (لعلهم يرجعون) يردون البضاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers mean that if Jacob sends Benjamin, they will obtain their measure; otherwise they have been denied it.
rows.anchor: أي إن أرسلته معنا اكتلنا، وإلا فقد منعنا الكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob recalls that they gave the same assurance about Joseph, citing 12:12, so he distrusts their new promise.
rows.anchor: كذلك قلتم لي في يوسف: (أرسله معنا غدا يرتع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥafiẓan is read as a specification (tamyīz); ḥāfiẓan is read as a circumstantial accusative and may also be specification.
rows.anchor: وحفظا منصوب على التمييز، و (حافظا) منصوب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruddat is also read with kasra on rāʾ; its original doubled dāl is assimilated, and the kasra may be transferred from dāl as in qīla and bīʿa.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ ردت بكسر الراء، والأصل رددت

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub reports a dialect transferring a consonant’s kasra to the preceding consonant, as in ḍuriba Zayd; this also permits kabid/kibid.
rows.anchor: وقد حكى قطرب أنه يقال في ضرب زيد؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā nabghī can ask what more they want after their payment was returned, or deny that they want anything.
rows.anchor: أي ما نريد، وما في موضع نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Numīru means supplying provisions; each man received a camel-load, and that measure was easy for the person traveling to them.
rows.anchor: مرتهم أميرهم ميرا إذا أتيتهم بالمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illā an yuḥāṭa bikum means their return is excused only if they are surrounded and physically prevented from bringing Benjamin.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الإحاطة بهم، أنه يحال بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is a purpose/causal accusative; illā introduces a confirming condition, like “only to take the dirhams.”
rows.anchor: فموضع أن نصب، والمعنى لتأتنني به إلا لإحاطة بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob fears the evil eye; the evil eye is real, and a report says the Prophet sought protection for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn from every harmful eye.
rows.anchor: قد خاف عليهم العين، وأمر العين صحيح

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s reported protective prayer for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn asks refuge from every harmful eye.
rows.anchor: وأعيذكما من كل عين لامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The need in Jacob’s heart that he fulfilled was fear of the evil eye.
rows.anchor: أي إلا خوف العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God’s decree meant harm, it would reach the brothers whether together or apart; another possible meaning is that nothing can avert God’s decree.
rows.anchor: قدر أن تصيبهم لأصابتهم وهم متفرقون كما تصيبهم مجتمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ḥājatan is an exception not drawn from the preceding category, meaning “but a need in Jacob’s heart that he fulfilled.”
rows.anchor: ونصب حاجة استثناء ليس من الأول، المعنى لكن حاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob had knowledge because God taught him.
rows.anchor: أي لذو علم لتعليمنا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āwā ilayhi means that Joseph drew his brother close.
rows.anchor: (آوى إليه أخاه) أي ضم إليه أخاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā tabtaʾis means do not grieve or become distressed.
rows.anchor: (فلا تبتئس): أي لا تحزن ولا تستكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A caller announced the accusation; ādhantu means informed, while adhantu means making a repeated announcement.
rows.anchor: أي أعلم معلم، يقال آذنته بالشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “O caravan” addresses its people, as “ask the town” means ask its people; ayy is feminine because it refers to the feminine caravan.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الأصحاب للعير، ولكن قال: أيتها العير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vessel’s name is read ṣuwāʿ or ṣāʿ; Abū Hurayra read ṣāgh and another reading has ṣawgh.
rows.anchor: وقرئت " صواع الملك "، وقرئت " صاع الملك "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A camel’s load means a camel-load of food, and zaʿīm means guarantor.
rows.anchor: ولمن جاء به حمل بعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣuwāʿ is the same as ṣāʿ and either noun may be masculine or feminine; reports describe a long cup-shaped royal drinking vessel, made of silver overlaid with gold, copper, or shaped like a bowl.
rows.anchor: الضواع هو الصاع بعينه، وهو يذكر ويؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾallāh means wa-Allāh; tāʾ is used in oaths only with Allah, replacing wāw, as in turāth for wirāth and yattazin from yuwtazin.
rows.anchor: إلا أن التاء لا يقسسم بها إلا في (الله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny corruption because they did not wrong local people or let their camels graze others’ crops; they deny theft because they returned the payment found in their baggage.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا لا ينزلون على قوم ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The penalty among Jacob’s family was to enslave a thief, making him the property of the person whose goods he stole.
rows.anchor: وكان جزاء السارق عندهم أن يستعبد بسرقته، يصير عبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes jazāʾu as subject and man as predicate, with fa-huwa jazāʾuhu added for clarification, like repeating a thief’s penalty after naming it.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن هو جزاؤه ابتداء، ويكون من وجد في رحله الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, man wajada… fa-huwa jazāʾuhu is the predicate clause, whose resumptive pronoun refers to jazāʾ; Arabic repeats the noun itself to avoid ambiguity, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: هذه الجملة خبر الجزاء، والعائد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians cite an unattributed line repeating al-mawt rather than a pronoun to show this noun-resumption pattern.
rows.anchor: لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in istakhrajahā refers to al-siqāya, or alternatively treats ṣuwāʿ as feminine.
rows.anchor: رجع بالتأنيث على السقاية، ويجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king’s law required a thief to pay double what he stole; Jacob’s family law enslaved the thief to the victim.
rows.anchor: كان يغرم مثلي ما سرق، وكان عند آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In illā an yashāʾa Allāh, an is accusative after the omitted preposition bi; Joseph could take his brother only by God’s will.
rows.anchor: موضع (أن) نصب، لما سقطت الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darajāt may be genitive as an annexation to man, or accusative with man as object: God raises whomever He wills by degrees.
rows.anchor: على إضافة الدرجات إلى " من " ويجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising darajāt with nominative is good Arabic but has no known transmission, so it should not be recited without a valid report.
rows.anchor: ويجوز رفع درجات من نشاء، وهي حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegesis says that above every knowledgeable person is someone more knowledgeable, until knowledge reaches God.
rows.anchor: قيل في التفسير: فوق كل ذي علم عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joseph as a child took a golden image worshipped by people outside Islam, intending to denounce rather than venerate it.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنه كان في صغره أخذ صورة مما كان يتعبد به بعض من يخالف أهل ملة الإسلام من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “he concealed it” is explained by the words “you are worse in position”: they truly stole by taking their brother from their father.
rows.anchor: وهذا إضمار على شريطة التفسير، لأن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God knows best what you describe” means He knows whether Joseph’s brother actually stole.
rows.anchor: أي الله أعلم أسرق أخ له أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿazīz means the king.
rows.anchor: والعزيز الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaykhan modifies ab, and kabīran modifies shaykh.
rows.anchor: من نعت أب، وأب منصوب ب (إن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Joseph a benefactor asks him to act generously beyond strict obligation, since he fed them and returned their payment.
rows.anchor: أي ممن يحسن ولا يعامل بالتحديد في واجب لأنه كان أعطاهم الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿādh Allāh is an accusative verbal noun meaning “I seek refuge”; an naʾkhudha is accusative after min is omitted.
rows.anchor: منصوب على المصدر المعنى أعوذ بالله معاذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says taking anyone other than the person found with the goods would make them unjust.
rows.anchor: (إنا إذا لظالمون) أي إن أخذنا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaṣū najiyyan means they withdrew to confer about returning to their father without their brother; najī is singular in form but collective in meaning.
rows.anchor: المعنى خلصوا يتناجون، أي خلصوا متناجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collective expressions include qawm najī, qawm najwā, and qawm anjiya; an unattributed poem uses anjiyah to illustrate the form.
rows.anchor: إني إذا ما القوم صاروا أنجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaṣū also means they separated themselves, with Benjamin absent.
rows.anchor: ومعنى خلصوا انفردوا وليس معهم أخوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best parsing makes mā in wa-min qablu mā farraṭtum redundant, giving “and previously you failed concerning Joseph.”
rows.anchor: أجود الأوجه أن يكون (ما) لغوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā is nominative, meaning “your failure concerning Joseph previously”; or accusative coordinated with the earlier clause, meaning they knew of their failure.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما في موضع رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I will not leave the land” means Egypt, since everyone lives on land.
rows.anchor: أي لن أبرح أرض مصر، وإلا فالناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aw yaḥkuma Allāhu lī may coordinate with ḥattā yaʾdhana (“until God permits”) or answer lan (“I will not leave until God rules for me”).
rows.anchor: نسق على (حتى يأذن)، ويجوز أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active saraqa is the stronger reading; the passive suriqa can mean either that he was known to steal or was accused of stealing.
rows.anchor: إلا أن سرق آكد في القراءة، وسرق يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwalat means their souls adorned the deed and made it appealing to them.
rows.anchor: أي زينت لكم أنفسكم وحببت إليكم أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-ṣabrun jamīl means “my affair is beautiful patience” or “my patience is beautiful.”
rows.anchor: المعنى فأمري صبر جميل أو فصبري صبر جميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā asafā means “O my sorrow”; the possessive yā in yā asafī may become alif for ease.
rows.anchor: معناه يا حزناه، والأصل يا أسفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kazīm means grief-stricken.
rows.anchor: وقال يا أسفى على يوسف وابيضت عيناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafʾa means “you continue”; the oath has an omitted lā, so the sense is “by God, you will not stop mentioning Joseph.”
rows.anchor: معنى تالله: والله، و " لا " مضمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaraḍ can mean bodily corruption or illness, or moral corruption; aḥraḍahu ʿalā means he corrupted him against someone.
rows.anchor: والحرض الفاسد في جسمه، أي حتى تكون مدنفا مريضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted lā is allowed because an oath cannot say “you do” without an emphatic lām or a negative; oaths should be sworn only by God, never by parents or prophets.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاز إضمار " لا " في قوله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly told ʿUmar not to swear by fathers and said that whoever swears should swear by God.
rows.anchor: يروى عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال لعمر: لا تحلفوا

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans give several accounts for God’s oaths by created things: they point to God’s greatness, stand for “Lord of” those things, or mean their creation; the first is best.
rows.anchor: ففيها أوجه كلها قد ذكرها البصريون، فقالوا:

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub interprets oaths by sun or fig and olive as elliptical for “by the Lord of” those things, supported by other divine oaths.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب جائز أن يكون معناها: ورب الشمس وضحاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the proposed explanations for divine oaths by created things, al-Zajjāj prefers the first explanation: they show God’s greatness and signs.
rows.anchor: وأجود هذه الأقوال ما بدأنا به في أولها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mazjāt is explained as little; some say the brothers brought Bedouin goods such as wool and ghee, while others say the goods were unsuitable inferior food-trade items.
rows.anchor: قالوا (مزجاة) قليلة، وقالوا كانوا جاءوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, tazjiya is a small amount used to get by: one “gets through life” on little; the cited poem uses tuzjī for a mother pushing her children along.
rows.anchor: أن التزجية الشيء القليل الذي يدافع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses tuzjī to mean pushing along, describing a she-camel moving her young.
rows.anchor: الواهب المائة الهجان وعبدها. . . عودوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭiʾa/yakhṭaʾu and akhṭaʾa/yukhṭiʾu are distinct verb forms; an Imruʾ al-Qays line uses khaṭiʾna.
rows.anchor: قد خطئ يخطأ خطأ وخطأ، وأخطأ يخطئ إخطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob planned to seek forgiveness at the late-night dawn prayer, a time when supplication is answered, not because he was withholding forgiveness; this better suits prophetic character.
rows.anchor: إرادة أن يستغفر لهم في وقت وجه السحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āwā ilayhi abawayhi means Joseph embraced his parents.
rows.anchor: (آوى إليه أبويه). أي ضم إليه أبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿarsh is the throne; prostrating to Joseph was a customary act of honoring people at that time.
rows.anchor: كان من سنة التعظيم في ذلك الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they fell prostrate to God, not to Joseph.
rows.anchor: وقيل: (وخروا له سجدا) وخروا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in “You gave me of sovereignty” and “taught me of interpretation” may be partitive, meaning some sovereignty and some interpretation.
rows.anchor: جائز أن يكون أراد علمتني بعض التأويل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, min specifies the kind rather than a portion: God gave sovereignty and taught interpretation, as in 3:26 and 22:30.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون دخول " من " لتبين هذا الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāṭira may be an adjective of rabb, or a second vocative: “O Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector.”
rows.anchor: ينتصب على وجهين: أحدهما على الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Join me with the righteous” asks God to place Joseph among them in rank through mercy and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أي ألحقني بمراتبهم من رحمتك وغفرانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Joseph and his brothers was hidden from the Prophet; its revelation proves his prophethood and serves as warning and instruction through earlier peoples’ stories.
rows.anchor: المعنى الذي قصصنا عليك من أمر يوسف وإخوته من الأخبار التي كانت غائبة عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika may be the subject with min anbāʾ al-ghayb as predicate and nawḥīhi as a second predicate; alternatively nawḥīhi is the predicate and dhālika means “that which.”
rows.anchor: وموضع (ذلك) رفع بالابتداء ويكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people will not believe even if the Prophet strives to guide them; he cannot guide whom he loves, for God guides whom He wills, as 28:56 says.
rows.anchor: لأنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks no payment for reciting the Qurʾan or guiding people; it is a reminder of their welfare, salvation from Hell, entry to Paradise, warning, and good news.
rows.anchor: أي وما تسألهم على القرآن وتلاوته وهدايتك إياهم من أجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs in the unsupported sky, sun and moon, plants, seas, and mountains prove one Creator, yet people turn away without reflecting.
rows.anchor: أي من علامة ودلالة تدلهم على توحيد الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They acknowledge God as their creator and creator of heaven and earth but associate idols and other things with Him in worship.
rows.anchor: أي إن اعترفوا بأن الله خالقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gāshiya is an overwhelming punishment; baghtatan is a circumstantial accusative meaning that the Hour comes suddenly, when they do not expect it.
rows.anchor: أي أن يأتيهم ما يعجزهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may be al-dār al-ākhira, with ākhira modifying dār because people have two homes, or dār al-ākhira meaning the home of afterlife, as people have two lives; compare al-ṣalāt al-ūlā and ṣalāt al-ūlā.
rows.anchor: فمن قال الدار الآخرة فالآخرة نعت للدار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings kadh-dhibū and kudhibū differ: with gemination, the messengers despaired that their people would believe; with light consonants, their people thought the messengers had lied.
rows.anchor: قرئت كذبوا وكذبوا، بالتخفيف والتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that the messengers themselves thought God had failed them is remote and unbecoming of messengers.
rows.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم وظنوا أنهم قد أخلفوا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet was not given a promise that God failed to fulfill.
rows.anchor: يروى عن عائشة أن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says, “God forbid that the messengers should think this of their Lord”; the light reading may instead mean their people thought they were liars.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر: ومعاذ الله أن يظن الرسل هذا بربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rescue clause has readings fannunajjī, fanunajjī with a deleted nūn to avoid two nūns, fanajā as a past-tense continuation, and fanunjiya as passive past with man in nominative.
rows.anchor: قرئت فننجي، وفننجي، وقرئت فنجا من نشاء

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim read fanunji with fatḥa on yāʾ; the sense is that God rescued those He willed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم (فنجي من نشاء) بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ladhī bayna yadayhi means the scriptures that came before the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: أي الذي تقدمه من الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the accusative reading, taṣdīqan is coordinated with an understood kāna: the story was not invented but was confirmation of earlier scripture.
rows.anchor: ونصب " تصديقا " على معنى كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising taṣdīq and its coordinated words is good Arabic, but lacks sound transmitted recitation; do not recite it against consensus.
rows.anchor: وهذا لم تثبت بقراءته رواية صحيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥāna is an accusative verbal noun meaning “I glorify God”; tasbīḥ linguistically declares God free of evil, as in a Prophetic report.
rows.anchor: (سبحان) منصوب على المصدر، المعنى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asrā biʿabdihi laylan means He made His servant travel by night; asrā and sarā both mean night travel, as in 89:4.
rows.anchor: يقال أسريت وسريت إذا سرت ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God took the Prophet from Mecca—the whole sacred precinct counts as the mosque—to Jerusalem; rivers and fruit around Jerusalem explain its blessing.
rows.anchor: من المسجد الحرام وهو مكة، والحرم كله مسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-nuriyahu means “to show Muhammad”; that night God showed him prophets and their signs.
rows.anchor: فأراه الله في تلك الليلة من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet reported the approaching Syrian caravan’s arrival time and gray lead camel; Quraysh saw it arrive as stated but still did not believe.
rows.anchor: فأخبرهم أنها تقدم في يوم سماه لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book was guidance because it showed the Children of Israel the way.
rows.anchor: أي دللناهم به على الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not take a protector besides Me” means do not rely on anyone else or take another lord.
rows.anchor: أي لا تتوكلوا على غيري ولا تتخذوا من دوني ربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhurriyyata is read with fatḥa or kasra on dhāl, with ḍamma more common; most analyses parse it as a vocative, “O descendants of those We carried with Noah,” recalling rescue from the flood.
rows.anchor: القراءة بنصب (ذرية). وقرأ بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dhurriyyata is an object of tattakhidhū, with dhurriyya and wakīlan as its two objects; the descendants are not to be taken as protectors.
rows.anchor: ويجوز النصب على معنى ألا تتخذوا (ذرية)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nominative dhurriyyatu as a substitute for the subject pronoun is possible Arabic, but should not be recited without a sound transmission.
rows.anchor: ويجوز الرفع في (ذرية) على البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaḍaynā ilā means We informed or revealed to the Children of Israel, as in 15:66.
rows.anchor: معناه أعلمناهم في الكتاب، وأوحينا إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fa-qaḍāhunna sabʿa samāwāt, qaḍā means created and completed the heavens, as in 41:12.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (فقضاهن سبع سماوات في يومين) معناه خلقهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line uses qaḍāhumā of two coats of mail, meaning he made them; the cited form supports the sense of making.
rows.anchor: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما. . . داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root broadly means completing work decisively; a judge is called qāḍī because his order is not reversed, and qaḍā separates matters by firm resolution.
rows.anchor: كل ما عمل عملا محكما فقد قضي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised corruption and great elevation mean they would become tyrannical and arrogant; every tyrant is described as having risen and exalted himself.
rows.anchor: معناه لتعظمن ولتبغن، لأنه يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first promise means the first of the two periods of corruption.
rows.anchor: المعنى فإذا جاء وعد أولى المرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that Bukhtanassar was the enemy sent against them.
rows.anchor: يروى أنه بعث عليهم بختنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāsū means they searched thoroughly through the homes to see whether anyone remained alive; jaws is searching exhaustively.
rows.anchor: أي فطافوا في خلال الديار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-karrata means the return of power; akthar nafīran means more supporters, or a collective plural like nafar; nafīran is specification (tamyīz).
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون نفيرا جمع نفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For li-yasūʾū, the promise may be the subject (“the promise makes your faces wretched”), or the people may be the subject (“these people make your faces wretched”); a light-nūn variant li-nasūʾ is also reported.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (ليسوءوا) فالمعنى ليسوء هؤلاء القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stronger forms are li-yasūʾa without nūn and li-yasūʾū; reading li-yasūʾ with the promise as agent in an imperative sense is allowed but should not be recited.
rows.anchor: والأجود ليسوء بغير نون، وليسوءوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light-nūn form li-nasūʾ may also occur with nūn replacing yāʾ.
rows.anchor: ويجوز لنسوء بالنون في موضع الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbirū means destroy; tabr is something shattered, and mā ʿalaw means while they hold the upper hand over you.
rows.anchor: معناه ليدمروا، ويقال لكل شيء منكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣīran means confinement or prison; the woven mat and the side of the body are also called ḥaṣīr because their parts are enclosed together.
rows.anchor: معناه حبسا، أخذ من قوله: حصرت الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most upright way is monotheism, bearing witness that none is god but God, believing His messengers, and obeying Him.
rows.anchor: أي للحال التي هي أقوم الحالات، وهي توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may angrily pray for evil against themselves, children, or family just as they pray for good; this is a human-wide trait, and al-insān here means people.
rows.anchor: أن الإنسان ربما دعا على نفسه وولده وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report tells how Sawda bint Zamʿa loosened a prisoner’s shackles after he complained, he escaped, and the Prophet prayed against her in anger; he explained that unjust curses from him are mercy for the undeserving and told her he is human and can become angry.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - رفع إلى سودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s statement that humanity was created hasty applies to all people, from Adam through the last of his descendants.
rows.anchor: فأعلم الله - عز وجل - أن الإنسان خلق عجولا
